title: Free or defended: who can really recapture? (part 3 of 3)
outcomes: Counts only the pieces that can capture on a square as its defenders
Decides whether a capture is free, wins points or loses points
Does not treat a nearby enemy piece as a defender
sources: items IG-CTRST-*, I-CAP-002, IBds11-9..12 and IBG-LFNDCAPTURE2-* (claims checked by tools/validate.py)

steps.text: Part 3 of 3: Free or defended: who can really recapture?. This part covers Check yourself. Each part is short on purpose: finish one, play a game or take a break, and come back.

steps.prompt: In two sentences, explain to a friend why a bishop standing next to a knight does not always defend it. Name one square where you once counted a defender that was not one.

steps.text: **Compare with your own words.** A piece is defended only if a friendly piece can really capture on its square: its own kind of move, with a clear line. A piece standing nearby, a bishop on the wrong square colour or a rook behind its own pawn does not count. If the target is defended, compare what you win with what you could lose.
